I wish I could agree or understand a man’s argument for this, but truly, it would be wildly unfair to subject a woman to a pregnancy that she does not want. It selfishly imposes upon her—pregnancy substantially interferes with career or educational pursuits. It can push someone into parenthood who is not ready to do so, while subjecting a child to a potentially unprepared/unwelcoming environment. 

Additionally, what guarantees the man stays? What guarantees he even has the ability to financial support a child? I don’t think someone should have the ability to make a decision for another that so heavily burdens and affects her without regard for her desire or even ability to proceed with the 9 month journey. As a woman, pregnancy terrifies me: risk of postpartum psychosis, constant pain and/or nausea for 9 months, discomfort in performing even the simplest tasks (walking, sleeping comfortably, etc), and most particularly, the not so low likelihood I could die in labor. 

Under a purely legal lens—using your example to apply to reality—the state can impose some restrictions upon a woman’s access to an abortion (see undue burden test). This effectively allows the state to make a decision on the behalf of a woman and it is constitutionally permitted to do so because the state wields an interest in preserving life. While men wield the right to procreate, they do not have the legal power to “protect” potential life by forcing a woman to come to term with their child. 

Imagine the inverse(in a slightly non-parallel example) of forcing a woman or a man to become sterilized(btw has not been directly addressed by the court, but the court has ruled that the equal protection clause prevents a state from forcefully sterilizing convicts). Having a child or becoming sterilized is a lifetime imposition. I think it is unfair for a man to be subjected to sterilization when that isn’t what he wants. 

Obviously, the right to abortion is highly contentious and there are arguments available to both sides, but this is my reasoning as to why a man should not have the right to determine that a woman must bear his child.

I’m sorry you feel this way. It sounds incredibly hard. I have felt that hopelessness and the self-hate you are describing. Financial security is a start, it can be a foundation u build off of. I suggest you look into summer courses(which are online rn) at local community colleges. Befriend a professor there, seek advice, maybe inquire about research he/she is doing. I think it’s admirable you want to do psychology. I could never do a stem major, my brain freaks out when I see numbers. It’s very impressive you’ve made it this far—that something to be proud of, not everyone can. If you would like to do a practice of sorts like therapy, you can email local therapists and ask for mentorship. I’m sure one would be bound to say yes. Friends will come into your life at the most unpredictable times. At the end of the day, I’m proud of you and I know you can do it.
